title: Living in San Carlos, CA: The Complete Guide

items.html: Living in San Carlos, California

San Carlos sits halfway between San Francisco and San Jose, between Belmont and Redwood City. It calls itself the City of Good Living, and the reasons are easy to list: top-ranked public schools, a walkable downtown on Laurel Street, a Caltrain station, hillside trails and parks in every neighborhood, and a calendar of hometown events that people actually go to. This guide puts what you need to know in one place, with links to the rest of San Carlos Life for the details.
Neighborhoods · Schools · Getting around · Downtown · Parks · Events · Homes · Questions

San Carlos is small enough to cross in ten minutes, but each part of town feels different. The flatlands near downtown have tree-lined streets of older bungalows within walking distance of Laurel Street and the train. The hills to the west trade that walkability for quiet streets, larger lots and views of the Bay.

  • Howard Park: closest to downtown, Burton Park and Caltrain.
  • El Sereno & White Oaks: residential streets southeast of downtown.
  • Clearfield Park: around the Caltrain station, east of El Camino Real.
  • Cordes: the northern hills by Arguello Park.
  • Beverly Terrace: hillside homes near Big Canyon and Crestview parks.
  • Alder Manor: the southern hills, with views across the Bay.

Click a neighborhood on the map to open its page.

The San Carlos School District runs the town's public schools from kindergarten through eighth grade. Children start at one of four lower elementary schools (Arundel, Brittan Acres, Heather or White Oaks), move to Arroyo or Mariposa for grades 4 and 5, and finish at Central or Tierra Linda middle school. San Carlos Charter Learning Center, the first charter school in California, is also part of the district.

For high school, students go on to the Sequoia Union High School District, most often Carlmont High School in Belmont or Sequoia High School in Redwood City.

School assignments follow your address, so check the district's school locator before you choose a home.

The historic San Carlos Caltrain station

items.html:
Caltrain stops at the historic San Carlos depot, a short walk from Laurel Street. Electric trains have run the corridor since September 2024, with faster and more frequent service to San Francisco, Palo Alto and San Jose. Caltrain's own headquarters is in San Carlos.

By car, US-101 runs along the east side of town and I-280 along the hills to the west, so both the Bay side and the Peninsula's spine are minutes away. El Camino Real crosses the city north to south.

San Carlos Airport serves small planes, and the Hiller Aviation Museum sits beside it. Commercial flights leave from SFO to the north or San Jose to the south.

Downtown San Carlos runs along Laurel Street and San Carlos Avenue, with most shops and restaurants owned by local people. You'll find cuisines from around the world, coffee and gelato, bookstores, toy shops and a long-running music store, and the car-free 700 block of Laurel Street is set up for dining outdoors.

Every Sunday the farmers market fills Laurel Street from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m.

items.alt: Mark Martinho and Viv Kelvin on Laurel Street in downtown San Carlos
Frank D. Harrington Park in downtown San Carlos

items.html:
The City looks after 17 parks, from Burton Park in the middle of town (playgrounds, ball fields, summer concerts and movies) to hillside open space with hiking trails in Big Canyon, Eaton and Crestview parks. Edgewood Park and Natural Preserve and Pulgas Ridge are a short drive away, and Filoli's gardens are in nearby Woodside.

The climate is mild and Mediterranean: dry, sunny summers, cool wet winters and no snow, so the parks get used all year.

• Every Sunday: farmers market on Laurel Street.
  • May: Hometown Days, the town's festival and parade since 1979.
  • Summer: Music in the Park on Friday nights and movies at Burton Park.
  • October: the Art and Wine Faire downtown on the first weekend.
  • December: the Night of Holiday Lights and Christmas Tree Lane on Eucalyptus Avenue.

items.html:
San Carlos has about 11,894 homes, most of them single-family houses on quiet residential streets, with condos and townhomes closer to El Camino Real and downtown. Good schools and the location between San Francisco and Silicon Valley keep demand steady, and homes in popular neighborhoods often sell quickly.

Prices change month to month, so look at current listings and recent sales rather than averages. Viv Kelvin and Mark Martinho of Vabrato Real Estate live and work here and can walk you through any neighborhood.

items.title: Is San Carlos a good place to live?
items.html: For many families, yes: highly rated K–8 public schools, low-key neighborhoods, a walkable downtown, Caltrain and quick freeway access, and parks across town. The trade-off is cost, as with most of the Peninsula.

items.title: Where is San Carlos?
items.html: On the San Francisco Peninsula in San Mateo County, about halfway between San Francisco and San Jose, between Belmont and Redwood City.

items.title: Which schools serve San Carlos?
items.html: The San Carlos School District (kindergarten to grade 8) and, for high school, the Sequoia Union High School District, usually Carlmont or Sequoia High School. Your address decides the school.

items.title: How do people commute from San Carlos?
items.html: Many take Caltrain from the San Carlos station; others drive US-101 or I-280. Downtown is walkable from the neighborhoods nearest the station.

items.title: Which neighborhood is closest to downtown?
items.html: Howard Park, followed by El Sereno & White Oaks and Clearfield Park. The hill neighborhoods (Cordes, Beverly Terrace, Alder Manor) are a short drive up.

items.title: What is there to do on a weekend?
items.html: The Sunday farmers market, lunch on Laurel Street, a hike in the hillside parks, the Hiller Aviation Museum, or one of the town's seasonal events.
